newsitem.title: USA: F-16 fighter jet crashes in New Mexico.
newsitem.headline: F-16 fighter jet crashes in New Mexico.

text.p: An Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed in an isolated area of New Mexico Monday but the pilot ejected safely and no one was killed or injured, officials said.

Air Force Staff Sgt. Gayle Ornong said the F-16C fighter crashed at 9:40 a.m. about five miles north of Vaughn, N.M., while on a routine training flight from the Cannon Air Force Base 110 miles (175 km) away in eastern New Mexico.
"There was only one person on board. He ejected from the aircraft and is uninjured," Ornong said, adding that the cause of the accident was being investigated by Air Force experts.

Officials said the F-16C, which was flying as part of a four-jet formation at the time of the accident, came down in a remote area north of Vaughn, about 90 miles (140 km) southeast of Albuquerque, and caused no damage or injuries on the ground.
Chris Evans, a spokesman at Cannon Air Force Base, said the plane, which cost $12.8 million, was destroyed. The pilot was taken to hospital for medical checks but suffered no injuries.
